q1: SELECT O1.SEAT_ID FROM CINEMA O1 WHERE O1.FREE = 1 AND ((SELECT FREE FROM CINEMA O2 WHERE O2.SEAT_ID = O1.SEAT_ID - 1) = 1 OR (SELECT FREE FROM CINEMA O2 WHERE O2.SEAT_ID = O1.SEAT_ID + 1) = 1)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT A.SEAT_ID FROM CINEMA AS A JOIN CINEMA AS B WHERE ABS(A.SEAT_ID-B.SEAT_ID)=1 AND A.FREE=TRUE AND B.FREE=TRUE ORDER BY A.SEAT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 returns seat IDs where the seat is free AND at least one of the adjacent seat (SEAT_ID-1 or SEAT_ID+1) is also free. Q2 returns distinct seat IDs where both the seat and its adjacent seat are free, meaning it finds pairs of adjacent free seats. Q1 includes a seat if either neighbor is free, whereas Q2 requires both neighbors to be free for the pair to be returned.
counterexample_dsp: A test database where seat 1 is free, seat 2 is not free, and seat 3 is free. Q1 will return seat 1 and 3 (since each has a free adjacent seat), but Q2 will return no results (no adjacent pair with both free).
